definition: A durable advantage that keeps competitors from taking a business's customers or margins, such as switching costs, scale economies, supply access or network effects. In this repo a moat is judged by how long and how much it would cost a buyer or rival to get around it.

This repo's 1-5 judgement of how hard it is to get around NVIDIA in one stack layer: 1 = commoditised or NVIDIA behind, 3 = rivals at parity on some dimensions while NVIDIA leads on integration, 5 = no rival close and switching takes years. A synthesis of each layer page's verdicts, not a measured quantity.
Whether NVIDIA's lead over the strongest challenger in a layer has been widening, stable or narrowing over roughly the last twelve months, as judged on that layer's competition page.

The profit available in one part of an industry's value chain (for example HBM, switch silicon or rack assembly), and who captures it. A layer can be strategically vital yet a small value pool for the company that controls it.
The ability to raise or hold prices without losing volume. For NVIDIA it shows up as a ~75% gross margin; rivals and in-house chips limit it first at the largest buyers.
